page.layout: One page of text. Running head at top with page number at top right. Two short poems, each under its own heading, set in full width in the centre of the page. A stray letter fragment at the left edge of the first heading is not printed text.

l.i: Roma olim cessit soceri generique furori,
Et gladiis cecidit Martia Roma suis:
Quod si illi placidas iunxissent fœdere dextras,
Robore staret adhuc Martia Roma suo.
Sic fratrum immitis nuper discordia pene
Funditus Europa verterat imperium:
At quoniam iungunt concordia pectora fratres,
Seruatum Europa dicitur imperium.
Sincerиc mos est nunquam neglectus amicis,
Anni sub primos mittere dona dies.
Nempe quod, ut veteris renouatur circulus anni,
Fas sit ut antiquus sic renouetur amor.
Ergo quum Bezam Truchius fateatur amicum,
Nec me Dampetrus deneget esse suum:
Non temere antiquos mores imitatus, utrique
Parua quidem mitto dona, sed apta tamen.
Ambo estis Cates [?], ambobus carmina dono,
Carmina, quae nostri pignus amoris erunt.
Vos pridem sincerus amor coniunxit in unum,
Vnum igitur decuit munus habere duos.

page.notes: Head of the second poem: "TRV-chio" hyphenated across the line. "Cates" in the line "Ambo estis Cates" is doubtful. The first letter of "Sincerиc" and of the first poem, both large initials, are read as likely letters. The first heading's stray "E" at the left edge is not transcribed.
